simplicity-r1-f1.rationale: Defending the `prune.thresholds` config knobs (R2 / R3 / R5) with cited evidence. Interview Round 1 records the user explicitly editing the AI's recommended threshold shape — line 35 of `007-prune-skill-interview.md`: *'Also: thresholds should be configurable in `admin/config.json` under `prune.thresholds` so projects on different cadences can tune; defaults match the AI's numbers.'* The configurability is the user's named ask during grilling, not AI-fabricated speculative configurability. Round 1 (line 33) also records the user's reasoning for tuning: 'The dormancy threshold for rules is too aggressive for non-negotiable rules' — the user's own taste-testing of the defaults was the surface that drove the configurability ask. Dropping `prune.thresholds` would re-introduce the very rigidity the user pushed back on during the interview. The Simplicity sub-clause 'no flexibility that wasn't requested' has its bite released here — the flexibility WAS requested, by name, with a concrete reason. **Concession on `prune.archiveRetention`.** The reviewer's point on the retention knob is valid in part — the v1 contract is forever-by-default and the knob exists primarily to surface a v2 enhancement path. Interview Round 3 (line 53) supports the slot's existence ('The knob exists so the v2 conversation has a slot but cannot fire today — speculative configurability prevented by the validation') but the reviewer's point that 'a knob whose v1 surface is a refusal message' is itself speculative configurability is well-aimed. Concession: drop `prune.archiveRetention` from R7 entirely. Move it to Open Questions as a v2 candidate. **Concession on `prune.staleLockMinutes`.** R8 already names this as a v2-promotion candidate, not a v1 knob — so it is already in the shape the reviewer recommends. No change needed. **Net effect:** push back on `prune.thresholds` (interview-grounded user ask); accept the concession on `prune.archiveRetention` (move to Open Questions); confirm `prune.staleLockMinutes` is already in the recommended shape. The push-back targets the load-bearing 80% of the finding; the concession addresses the 20% the reviewer is right about.
simplicity-r1-f1.revision_applied: R2, R3, R5 retain the `prune.thresholds` config knobs with documented defaults — the configurability is the user's named specification from Round 1. R7 edited to drop the `prune.archiveRetention` config knob entirely; v1 is forever-by-default with no config slot; the knob's v2 enhancement path is moved to Open Questions. R8's `prune.staleLockMinutes` framing as a v2 promotion candidate is unchanged (already in the recommended shape).

surgical-r1-f1.rationale: Asymmetric mutation surface is real. Four surfaces with four different Stage-2 mutation shapes is a maintenance-and-validation surface that grows with surface count; decision-log already demonstrates the cleanest pattern (Stage 2 read-only; archive file is single source of truth). Both proposed shapes are clean, but option (a) (uniform Stage-2 read-only across all four surfaces) preserves the user's Round 6 intent and extends the cleanest pattern across the corpus. The cost — Phase 3 consumers must learn to read the archive file as a filter — is paid once and applies uniformly; the alternative is paid four times bespoke per surface. **Caveat for option (a): agent snapshots.** The agent snapshot file at `admin/agents/specialised/{name}.md` is referenced by `agents/index.json` and loaded by every skill that uses the agent at runtime. A pure read-only Stage 2 (don't move the file, don't drop the index entry) would mean a 'pruned' agent is still active at runtime — that defeats the purpose of pruning. So agent snapshots specifically need Stage-2 mutation (move file + drop index entry) because the live registry IS the runtime surface. The asymmetry is structural, not bespoke. Going with a refined option (a): apply uniform read-only Stage-2 to decision-log, rules, and task-history (three surfaces; the archive file is single source of truth + Phase 3 consumers cross-reference); keep bespoke Stage-2 mutation for agent snapshots (the live registry is the runtime surface; pruning means removing-from-runtime). Three of four surfaces consolidate; one stays bespoke for a structural reason that's now documented.
surgical-r1-f1.revision_applied: R12 Stage 2 rewritten to apply uniform read-only treatment to three surfaces (decision-log, rules, task-history) — Stage 2 is a no-op write for these surfaces; the archive file is the single source of truth for archive state; Phase 3 consumers cross-reference the archive file. Stage 2 retains bespoke mutation for agent snapshots only — the live registry is the runtime surface, so pruning means moving the snapshot file and dropping the index entry. AC-11 updated to verify the three-surface read-only treatment plus the agent-snapshot mutation. The asymmetry from four bespoke shapes is collapsed to three-uniform-plus-one-structural-exception, with the exception's rationale named in R12. Surgical scope creep eliminated for three of four surfaces; the structural agent-snapshot exception is documented.

tbc-r1-f1.rationale: Unstated assumption is real. The PRD silently picked title-based citation detection without accounting for the existing convention in the worked example (`PREFER_LOCAL_TESTS` cites by date 2026-02-14; `PREFER_COMPOSITION_OVER_INHERITANCE` cites by date 2026-01-08). Title-based detection produces zero candidates against the existing rules — false negative. The proposed shape (a) — tolerate both citation styles — is the smaller surgical change. A citation-resolution helper extracts both quoted titles AND `YYYY-MM-DD` dates from rule bodies; for date-extracted refs, find the matching decision-log entry by `**Date:**` field and check supersession against that entry's title (since the supersede-link prefix IS title-based per `specflow:decision`'s R6 + AC-5). The bridge between date-based citations and title-based supersede-links is the citation-resolution step. Going with option (a).
tbc-r1-f1.revision_applied: R3 edited to name the citation-resolution strategy explicitly: 'A non-negotiable rule's body's *Why* section may cite a `decision-log.md` entry by title (quoted) OR by date (`YYYY-MM-DD` format); the skill's citation-resolution helper extracts both forms — for title citations, the rule cites the decision-log entry whose H2 title matches the quoted string; for date citations, the rule cites the decision-log entry whose `**Date:**` field matches the date. Once resolved to a decision-log entry's title, supersession detection is title-based per `specflow:decision`'s R6 + AC-5.' AC-3 updated to enumerate the citation-resolution helper's two extraction patterns. The block is resolved; the bridge between the existing date-based convention and the title-based supersede signal is named explicitly.

goal-r1-f1.rationale: Reverse-traceability gap is real. The byte-identical-capture mechanism is verified at write time but the round-trip restoration property — the goal-eval contract per SKILLS.md line 190 'pruning is reversible (archive retained)' — is not stated as an R-level contract. A fresh agent could implement R12 correctly at the mechanism level (capture is byte-identical) but produce an archive shape whose round-trip restoration breaks (e.g. fenced-code-block delimiter swallowing if the original entry contained backticks). Option (b) is the smaller surgical edit — keep R12 as the single requirement covering Stage 1 + Stage 2 but explicitly name the round-trip restoration as the contract Stage 1's byte-identical capture establishes. Option (a) (split R12 into R12 + R13) is cleaner architecturally but has more downstream wiring; option (b) closes the gap with a sentence and a corresponding AC-level verification.
goal-r1-f1.revision_applied: R12 rewritten to name round-trip restoration as the R-level contract: 'Round-trip restoration: a future user pasting a single archive block's `Original entry` content back into the source surface MUST reproduce the source registry's pre-archive state byte-for-byte for that entry — the byte-identical capture at Stage 1 is the surface that makes restoration deterministic.' AC-11 extended to verify the round-trip restoration property by literal restoration test (capture pre-archive bytes, run prune, run restoration via paste-back, diff against pre-archive bytes). The orphan-AC gap is closed; the goal-eval contract is now stated as an R-level contract.

da-r1-f1.rationale: Coverage gap on R8's edge cases is real. The `--force-unlock` race window produces a confused user state (force-unlock followed by cron-capture before re-invoke), and the hours-scale clock-skew case silently invalidates the lock semantics in two distinct ways (battery-failed past clock allows concurrent runs; misconfigured-timezone future clock makes the lock un-removable). Both proposed extensions are well-shaped and both are needed — the marker-file pattern for the force-unlock race resolves the priority question deterministically; the 24-hour-past / 1-hour-future bounds catch the actual failure mode (hours-scale skew, not seconds-scale). Extending R8 with both edge cases and updating AC-8 to enumerate them is the right shape — small edit, both cases closed at both R and AC level.
da-r1-f1.revision_applied: R8 extended with the marker-file pattern for `--force-unlock` race: after force-unlock removes the lock, the skill writes a one-line marker file at `admin/scratch/prune-{YYYY-Q}.unlock-marker` containing the unlock timestamp; the next `/prune` invocation reads the marker; if its timestamp is within 5 minutes of now, the invocation has priority and any concurrent cron-path that would otherwise create a lock between unlock and re-invoke must defer. The marker is consumed by the next manual `/prune` invocation OR auto-expires after 5 minutes. R8 also extended with the implausible-timestamp refusal: lock-body timestamps more than 24 hours in the past or more than 1 hour in the future are treated as corrupt; refuse with the implausible-timestamp sentinel. AC-8 extended to enumerate both edge cases (force-unlock-marker priority window + implausible-timestamp refusal).
